text:
Samira (People Ops): hey team — quick Q about booking an Airbnb for a 4-person trip to SF next month. One of us can book on a personal card and we'll split the cost. What's the reimbursement process and what receipts do we need? :thinking:

Alex (Eng): we usually do split charges on Venmo but for work i'd rather expense it. if i book w/ my personal card can i submit one expense with 4 names?

Jordan (Finance): short answer: OK if pre-approved and properly documented, but we need an itemized receipt that shows the full booking and a note that names/portion breakdown are attached. Finance won't reimburse a vague "split between 4" screenshot alone.

Samira (People Ops): to add — please use the company travel portal for hotels when possible. For Airbnbs specifically: either book on the company card (preferred) or, if personal card used, attach the host invoice + a short explanation and the split math. Manager approval required if total > $500 or if it's outside policy (multi-week stays).

Priya (Manager): FYI — i approved the trip, but please file expense before you leave if possible. If someone pays, add me as approver when you submit.

Alex (Eng): got it. what's the required proof for nightly rate vs cleaning/service fees? Airbnb lumps fees — do we need a breakdown?

Jordan (Finance): we need the full host invoice (the Airbnb confirmation email or PDF is fine) showing line items. If the host only shows a lump sum, include a screenshot of the booking details page and a short note explaining which portion is work-related. Taxes and cleaning fees are reimbursable as part of the lodging expense.

Lina (ExpenseBot): reminder: receipts must be attached as PDFs or clear screenshots. For reimbursements > $75, we need itemized receipts. For shared bookings, add a one-line CSV or table in the expense description: "Alex: $120, Priya: $120, Jordan: $120, Samira: $120" — this speeds up processing.

Samira (People Ops): also note per-diem rules: if you claim per-diem for meals, you cannot claim individual meal receipts for the same meals. You can either claim actuals (attach receipts) or daily per-diem (no meal receipts needed). Travel day partial per-diem follows the standard chart in the travel policy doc.

Alex (Eng): thanks — can expenses-bot link the travel policy?

expenses-bot: Here is the travel & expenses policy: https://redwood.company/docs/travel-expenses (contains per-diem table, pre-approval form, and Airbnb guidelines) :link:

Jordan (Finance): one more thing — have the person who paid include a short note in the expense like "paid by Alex personal card; reimb to Alex; split: Priya/Jordan/Samira/Team" so our ledger tags correctly. Finance will reimburse to the payer's bank/card on file.

Samira (People Ops): great — i'll update the quick FAQ in the travel channel and pin a mini checklist: 1) prefer company card 2) if personal card, attach host invoice + booking page 3) add split breakdown 4) manager approval for >$500 5) pick per-diem vs actuals. Thanks! :tada:
